note: Hand-authored. The one-way rule reference graph: an exception names the rule it overrides or extends; a base rule names nothing. Generated indexes under datasets/rules-reference/ and datasets/rules-packs/ are rebuilt from PDFs on every harvest and deliberately carry no reference field, so authored edges live here and only here. Each edge records why, because a plausible-but-wrong relationship is the failure mode this corpus exists to eliminate. Reverse lookup is computed at query time by tools/rules/refs.py and never stored. See docs/rules-provenance.md.

rr:overkill.why: Base damage application places damage on the character it was dealt to and nothing transfers. Overkill adds a transfer of the excess to the villain or the controlling identity.

rr:piercing.why: Tough prevents damage. Piercing discards tough status cards from the attacked character before damage is dealt, so it removes the prevention rather than the damage.

rr:tough.why: A tough status card cancels the damage a character would take, which is an exception to base damage application.

rr:guard.why: Base rules let a hero or ally attack any enemy that can be attacked. Guard removes the villain from that set while the guarding minion is engaged.

rr:quickstrike.why: Minions activate during step two of the villain phase. Quickstrike makes a minion attack on engaging, outside that step.

rr:surge.why: Step four reveals the cards a player was dealt. Surge adds another card to that process when the card carrying it is revealed.

rr:villainous.why: A basic power is used at its printed value. Villainous gives the character a boost card whose icons modify that value for the activation.

rr:assault.why: A basic thwart removes threat equal to the character's THW. Assault substitutes ATK for THW against a scheme carrying the keyword.

rr:stalwart.why: Status cards may be given to a character. Stalwart forbids the confused and stunned ones outright.

rr:steady.why: A character cannot hold more than one status card of each type. Steady raises that limit by one for confused and for stunned.

rr:stun-stunned.why: A character may use its basic attack power. A stunned status card cancels the next such attack and removes itself instead.

rr:confuse-confused.why: A character may use its basic thwart power. A confused status card cancels the next thwart and removes itself instead.

rr:retaliate-x.why: An enemy attack resolves against the defender. Retaliate adds damage back to the attacker after it does.

rr:crisis-icon.why: Threat is removed from a scheme by thwarting and by card effects. A crisis icon in play forbids player cards from removing it from the main scheme.

rr:acceleration-icon.why: Step one places the main scheme's printed acceleration threat. Each acceleration icon in play adds one more.

rr:peril.why: Players may normally consult and resolve together. Peril requires the resolving player to act alone, without table talk.
